verdicts.label: TRUE
verdicts.what_is_true_en: India's Chandrayaan-3 mission successfully landed in the Moon's south polar region on August 23, 2023, making it the first country to achieve a soft landing in that area. While the exact definition of 'near the south pole' is debated by some, the landing is widely recognized as a historic first for the southern lunar region.
verdicts.reasoning_en: Multiple high-quality sources, including NASA (ws-4), The Guardian (ws-2), and PBS (ws-3), confirm that India's Chandrayaan-3 was the first mission to successfully land near the Moon's south pole on August 23, 2023. A fact-check from BOOM (fc-1) also supports this by debunking a rival claim. While some sources (ws-7, ws-6) cite a scientist who disputes how 'near' the landing was to the pole based on a strict definition, the overwhelming consensus among space agencies and news organizations is that this was a historic first landing in the lunar south pole region.

verdicts.label: TRUE
verdicts.what_is_true_en: The Vikram lander from the Chandrayaan-3 mission successfully touched down on the Moon on August 23, 2023. The landing time is consistently reported as 18:03 or 18:04 local time in India (approximately 12:33-12:34 GMT).
verdicts.reasoning_en: Multiple reliable sources confirm the landing time of the Vikram lander. PBS (ws-11) and Global News (ws-9) report the touchdown at 6:04 p.m. local time. The Guardian (ws-10) states it was shortly after 6 p.m. (12:30 BST). Wikipedia (ws-8) and Space.com (ws-14) specify the time as 18:03/18:04 IST (12:33 UTC/GMT). The slight one-minute variation across sources is minor and they all corroborate the claim.
